name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz restricted; Iran says supertanker sank
summary: Iran's IRGC says a supertanker with 2m barrels sank near Hormuz on 15 Nov after a mine strike; claim unconfirmed
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on 15 Nov that two tankers on an unauthorised route in the southern Strait of Hormuz hit naval mines and that a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude sank; there was no independent confirmation (AFP via RTÉ). UKMTO said it was aware of an Indian report of a tanker attack in the Gulf, with the crew safe, but could not link it (Gulf News). Iran has restricted Hormuz traffic since the war began in late February, following claims of mine strikes on 13 and 14 Nov, so materially impeded Hormuz traffic sets the Alert.
for_you: Crews and shipping firms should follow UKMTO and JMIC advisories for the Gulf. Oil, gas and goods shipped via the Gulf face delays and higher insurance and freight costs.
rubric_hit: Alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded (Iranian route restrictions, repeated mine strike claims 13–15 Nov)

sources.title: RTÉ (AFP) — Iran says supertanker carrying oil sinks in Hormuz Strait
Gulf News — Iran says supertanker with 2 million barrels of oil sank in Gulf
Al Jazeera — Iran says tankers struck in Hormuz amid fears of new US attack

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
